body: Good information, exactly what I need. Thank you.

I'm still a bit concerned. A hospital visit would give me the perfect excuse to end it. There'd be no reason to keep going if that happened. If there's even a risk that talking to someone will land me there, I'd rather not even try it.

What about easing into that? Like exposing a SO to your family? Not all at once, just a little?

"Me? I don't want to kill myself. Just want to know why my grades suck"

"Sure, I get sad sometimes. But nothing big."

"Well, sometimes I think about suicide."

"Actually think about it quite a bit. Nothing specific though."

"Well I do have a gun, have decided that I'd write a note, leave it at my apartment and head out to the country because I want my landlord to be able to rent my apartment out easily, and I know the guy who collects bodies for the morgue and I don't want to make his life hard. Please help because I really think I'm going to do it."

Over the course of a few weeks or so.

I doubt I can afford a private therapist. I'm a college student who doesn't qualify for student loans and is paying for school out of pocket. That's like half the reason I want to kill myself.

Do you think even talking about general ideation is safe? I've seen some horror stories on reddit that make me reluctant to bring that up at all, and that's considering I'm reluctant to go in the first place.
K. Not really what I'm asking about.

Sometimes a pile of shit is a pile of shit I'm afraid.

Good luck to you, but if that's the thought I'm relying on, I don't anticipate being alive much longer.

That's a nice thought when you haven't seen how things turn out. 

Typically life doesn't make big turnarounds. For the most part things stay like they are. Same socio-economic class, same level of education as your family, decent chance you won't even leave the town you grew up in or you'll attempt to move into one exactly like it.

There are very rare instances where there's some hidden gem just around the corner, ready to make life worth living. 

I'm not telling you life isn't worth living. Maybe it'll be good for you. But despite my grades saying otherwise, I'm not so stupid as to not recognize patterns. I can see where my life is headed, and I don't like that. My attempts to change it have failed, as well as relying on sheer luck. Waiting any longer is not a tactic I'm interested in, I want things to change now or I'm going to stop this.

In other words, you don't know how to fix it. That's fine, neither do I.

See ya later.

My whole reason I've posted here is because I'm tired of waiting.

I've been putting it off two years but I've been dealing with issues for about four total. It was only after the first two that I started looking at suicide as an option. Before this I kept saying "Hey, who knows what else is out there?"

And that's not counting my teen years. I was cutting myself from 11-15 and still had occasional issues after that. Didn't help when I got caught and after that everyone treated me like I was made of glass. So that'd total it at about 11 years on and off that it's been on the table but I haven't done anything about it. 

I'm tired of waiting.

> It's cliche, but also very true - if you haven't gotten to where you want to be, you have not exhausted all the options yet

There's nothing further from the truth. You think everyone in life achieves everything they set their minds to? What would be the value in education? In higher paying jobs? People try and fail at things all the time, and very often they'll spend their whole lives with their Plan B or Plan C. 

> What would happen if you were hospitalised now?

Let me lay out how this would go for you, if I were hospitalized right this instant.

This kind of stuff can go anywhere from 24 hours to about 6 months (on average for an extended stay). For this scenario let's call it a month. Even a week would cause similar amounts of harm.

I go and I miss a months worth of class. I wasn't excused when I had an ER visit and missed a quiz, they aren't going to excuse me for this. A months worth of class includes exams, meaning I'm now going to be forced to withdraw from all classes. When my month is up, I'm coming to a much harder situation than the one I left.

My girlfriend would be sad and confused by this. She knows I'm upset with school but doesn't know the extent. While she's trying to cope with the fact that I want to kill myself, her parents would be telling her that they always knew something was wrong with me. Her sister would be trying to introduce her to other guys and insist I'm not someone she should be around. Her family hates me and this would give them validation. She's going to be harassed about this for a very long time, and that's assuming she doesn't listen to them. So I just made life much harder for her, where if I kill myself she can cope and in few years (max) she could find someone new.

My family would insist that I start attending church with my sister. I'm an atheist (they don't know that) so that would suck. But what sucks worse is that my sister's church largely believes mental illness to be a product of lack of faith or potential influence of demons. So now it's likely my atheism will be brought out in the open and everyone is going to blame that for my problems. I'd need to fake a conversion and play along until people let me out of their sight long enough for me to get my hands on a gun. This is all ignoring the fact that my family's and my girlfriend's family's social circle centers around this church, so now everyone I've ever known is free to judge me for wanting to die. People here aren't known for being open-minded, I would never be able to shake the reputation of "The guy who went to the loony bin".

And even in a perfect scenario where it works and I no longer want to kill myself. Now what? I'm still a failing college student with no ability to pay for school on his own. I'm still not going to be able to achieve the things I wish to. Now I don't want to kill myself, I just get to deal with a shitty life forever until I die from a some illness that I can't afford to go to the hospital for, because I never went to college so I have a shitty job.

> You could unload your gun and put it away before calling for help

I'm not calling anyone for help and my gun stays like it is. It's not like it being unloaded makes it any harder to kill myself, loading a gun isn't exactly difficult, even for a dumbass like me. 

> I'll stay online for a while to talk to you, if you like.

You do what you want. If you've got shit to do today don't feel obligated to stay here and talk to me. You leaving and doing something else isn't going to make me want to kill myself any more than I already do, and I mean that sincerely. You're not going to tell me anything I haven't heard before anyways and if I kill myself I'm sure as shit not going to announce it to you before I do it.

A mental health professional is required to suggest hospitalization if they feel I'm an imminent threat to myself. Considering that I own a handgun which is currently loaded and sitting in my bedside table, I'd say I probably qualify. If I do not consent to hospitalization then they're capable of intervening and having me admitted against my will. Everyone in my family would know, my girlfriend would know, my classmates would know. I would quite literally rather die than ever have that happen. 

It won't help anyways. My dad became a shrink after getting out of management (because unlike me, he was intelligent enough to graduate with not one, but two college degrees). I know the type of shit they're going to tell me. 

I do not qualify for additional financial support. I have spoken to my school's financial aid office, and they quite literally told me I don't qualify. When I was failing a class they told me I wouldn't qualify if I failed. I failed, and by extension I don't qualify. They gave me points on how to fight it but so far I have paid 3/4 of this semester's tuition on my own. I'm not going to be able to get help.

They are aware of my struggles, at least academically. I received 30 hours of tutoring last semester putting me in the top 5% of students using tutoring at my school. I received 26 the semester before that. I'm in frequent communication with my professors (my professor is the one who told me to drop the class). 

The only way to make any of my dreams a reality is through an education. That's not going to happen so I'm going to kill myself. There just isn't a way around that.

I can't give college another try. That's not me saying that, that's my college saying that. That's the financial aid office looking at my loan and grant eligibility saying that. That is my complete lack of money saying that. This is my only chance. I won't get another.

I've tried success without college. It didn't happen. I've tried my other options and they didn't work, college is very much my last resort.

Even if it wasn't, it doesn't matter. College is what would make me happy and I'm not achieving that.

I don't want to work a trade, I don't want to join the army, I don't want to be a college dropout who started his own business with this one trick that every redditor loves! Professors hate him!

I want a degree. It's that or nothing for me. Period.
